content:
I've spent some of the past month creating an interactive proof visualization tool Lean Graph.
The goal of this project is to increase the speed for understanding the structure of large proofs or namespaces.

The main components in the visualization are:

  • Graph where nodes are constants (theorems, definitions, etc...) and their respective construction dependencies are connected by edges
  • Force layout which groups related nodes together and keeps the graph readable
  • Coloring algorithm which increases pattern recognition for similarities among constants
  • Settings to adjust the readability of the visualization

Some examples can be directly opened in the app under File -> Open from server.
To visualize different graphs, you will need a specific .json file which can be opened under the File section.

To get the .json file for your custom project, follow these steps:

  1. Download DependencyExtractor.lean in the app under the File section
  2. Copy the downloaded file into your project and open it in VSCode (because of Lean language server)
  3. Using imports get access to the namespace or the constant (definition / theorem) that you want to create the graph for and at the bottom of the file you will find two #eval lines. Edit and uncomment one. This will create the .json file in the project folder

The project is open-source on GitHub.
